title: Beta blockers for peripheral arterial disease
authors: Paravastu SC, Mendonca DA, Da Silva A
population: Six randomised placebo-controlled trials of atenolol, propranolol, pindolol and metoprolol in people with intermittent claudication, reported between 1980 and 1991; search to March 2013
funder: Internal sources: none supplied. External sources: Chief Scientist Office, Scottish Government Health Directorates; the Cochrane Peripheral Vascular Diseases Group editorial base is supported by the Chief Scientist Office.
result: All six trials were small and of poor quality and no primary outcome was reported by more than one study, so results were not pooled. None showed a statistically significant worsening with beta-blockers of time to claudication, claudication distance or maximal treadmill walking distance, nor of calf blood flow, calf vascular resistance or skin temperature, and no adverse events were reported. The authors find no evidence of harm on walking distance and advise caution because large trials are lacking.
